tabs.title: Company Overview
tabs.content:
**Auralis Energy** is an electricity utility serving 1.4 million households. Smart meters installed at every property transmit a consumption reading every 30 seconds, producing a continuous stream of telemetry around the clock.

**Current Environment:**
- Meter readings currently land in nightly files that are loaded into an aging on-premises data warehouse once per day.
- Grid operators complain that they only discover demand spikes and outages many hours after they happen.
- Analysts export warehouse extracts to spreadsheets to build monthly consumption reports for regulators.

tabs.title: Requirements
tabs.content:
Auralis Energy is standardizing its analytics estate on **Microsoft Fabric** with these requirements:
- **Real-time visibility**: capture and process the smart-meter stream as readings arrive so grid operators can be alerted to demand spikes within seconds.
- **Unified storage**: keep one copy of raw meter files *and* curated tables in an open format that both Spark notebooks and SQL queries can work with, stored in OneLake.
- **Self-service reporting**: analysts should build interactive visuals showing consumption trends over time, replacing the spreadsheet exports.
